title: Section 498A misuse debate - what the Supreme Court has said lately
p1:
Is Section 498A really being “misused” — or is that label hiding a more complicated legal reality?

The Supreme Court’s recent approach suggests the answer is not simply yes or no.
p2:
A common misconception is that if a complaint appears exaggerated, the entire case automatically becomes false. That is not how the law works.

The Court has repeatedly recognized that allegations of cruelty under Section 498A must be examined carefully, while also cautioning against treating every matrimonial dispute as a criminal case.
p3:
One point many people miss: courts can intervene when criminal proceedings are clearly being abused, but that power is not meant to decide disputed facts at the very beginning.

In practice, the real question is whether the allegations, taken at face value, disclose an offence and whether continuing the case would amount to an abuse of the legal process.

That distinction matters for both complainants and accused persons.
conclusion: Do you think the present approach strikes the right balance between protecting genuine victims and preventing misuse of Section 498A?
